subject: history
topicDisplay: Changing Relations Northern Ireland Its Neighbours 1965 98
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which Northern Ireland civil rights organisation, formed in 1967, campaigned against discrimination?
questions.explain: NICRA was founded in 1967 to campaign for Catholic civil rights.

questions.q: Which 1974 power-sharing initiative collapsed after a loyalist workers' strike?
questions.explain: The 1973-74 Sunningdale Agreement collapsed after the 1974 Ulster Workers' Council strike.

questions.q: On Bloody Sunday in 1972, British soldiers shot dead civil-rights marchers in which city?
questions.explain: Bloody Sunday took place in Derry/Londonderry on 30 January 1972.

questions.q: The civil-rights movement of the late 1960s mainly campaigned against discrimination against which community?
questions.explain: The civil-rights movement protested discrimination against Catholics.

questions.q: A 1998 bombing that killed 29 people, the worst single Troubles atrocity, struck which town?
questions.explain: The Real IRA's Omagh bombing in August 1998 killed 29 people.

questions.q: The 1981 hunger strikes in the Maze prison were led by which republican prisoner?
questions.explain: Bobby Sands led the 1981 hunger strikes and died after 66 days.

questions.q: In which year was the Provisional IRA's long ceasefire first declared during the peace process?
questions.explain: The Provisional IRA announced a ceasefire in 1994, helping open the path to talks.

questions.q: In 1972 the British government suspended Stormont and imposed what form of government?
questions.explain: Direct Rule from Westminster was introduced in 1972.

questions.q: Which republican hunger striker was elected an MP shortly before dying in the Maze prison in 1981?
questions.explain: Bobby Sands was elected MP for Fermanagh and South Tyrone before dying on hunger strike in 1981.

questions.q: During the Second World War, what stance did Ireland (Eire) officially take?
questions.explain: Eire remained officially neutral throughout the Second World War.

questions.q: In which year were British troops first deployed onto the streets of Northern Ireland?
questions.explain: British troops were deployed to Northern Ireland in 1969 amid escalating violence.

questions.q: Which republican party, linked to the IRA, was led by Gerry Adams during the peace process?
questions.explain: Gerry Adams led Sinn Fein, associated with the IRA, during the peace process.

questions.q: Which 1985 agreement gave the Irish Republic a consultative role in Northern Ireland?
questions.explain: The 1985 Anglo-Irish Agreement gave Dublin a say in Northern Ireland affairs.

questions.q: What does 'IRA' stand for in the Northern Ireland conflict?
questions.explain: The IRA was the Irish Republican Army, a paramilitary group.

questions.q: In which year was the Good Friday (Belfast) Agreement signed?
questions.explain: The Good Friday Agreement was signed on 10 April 1998.

questions.q: Which Unionist leader and founder of the Democratic Unionist Party fiercely opposed compromise during the Troubles?
questions.explain: Ian Paisley, founder of the DUP, was a leading hardline Unionist voice during the Troubles.

questions.q: Which loyalist paramilitary group opposed the IRA during the Troubles?
questions.explain: The Ulster Volunteer Force was a loyalist paramilitary group.

questions.q: Which moderate nationalist leader shared the 1998 Nobel Peace Prize for his role in the peace process?
questions.explain: John Hume shared the 1998 Nobel Peace Prize with David Trimble.

questions.q: In which year did the Troubles escalate sharply, with British troops deployed and serious rioting in Derry and Belfast?
questions.explain: 1969 saw the Battle of the Bogside, widespread rioting and the deployment of British troops.

questions.q: The Good Friday Agreement of 1998 set up a power-sharing assembly based in which building?
questions.explain: The 1998 Agreement restored devolved government through the Stormont Assembly.

questions.q: What general name is given to the period of conflict in Northern Ireland from the late 1960s?
questions.explain: 'The Troubles' describes the decades of sectarian conflict.

questions.q: The 1916 rebellion in Dublin that shaped later Irish republicanism is known as what?
questions.explain: The 1916 Easter Rising in Dublin became a touchstone for Irish republicanism.
